title: Lightning from the ISS
dates: 2017–2023 (10-day roving window; the video opens on Mar 01 2017 and the year wheel ends at 2023)
description: Lightning flashes seen from the International Space Station. Each bright flash is one strike.

masks.note: Bottom-right control/annotation panel: date clock (0–66 s) and 10-day roving window year/month wheel (from ~68 s). Both are white text that would otherwise read as flashes.

extract.note: core = blown-out centre of a fresh strike: r,g ≥ 235, which admits both the audited reference white ≈ RGB(238,238,237) and the measured centres (255,255,66)–(255,255,153). halo = saturated yellow glow around it (measured (247,255,4)–(193,185,35); the reference yellow ≈ RGB(234,234,76) also passes). Stars, the ISS ground-track line and its label are bright but have no halo, so they never count. intensity is relative visual brightness only; there is no physical lightning-intensity colourbar in this visualization.

legend.means: where on Earth the flash is, west or east

_tuning: Sound numbers (octaves, voices, levels, filter, tension) are in js/sound/tuning.js.
